key_insight: Split-RL uses guidance labels to build gradient-boosted trees that separate locally conflicting learning signals instead of mixing them.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can use heuristic, sensor-event, or rule-based labels to structure learned policies around local tradeoffs such as speed versus precision.
method: Incorporate guidance labels into tree construction.
Route conflicting updates into disjoint state-space regions.
Analyze when early gradient aggregation loses objective-specific information and when the Split-RL score separates updates.
evidence_signal: Across constrained RL and mixed-dataset offline RL evaluations, the abstract reports meeting episodic cost budgets with competitive rewards and achieving near-expert offline performance across dataset sizes.
watch_item: Deployment requires suitable guidance labels; the abstract does not establish robustness to noisy or incomplete labels.
paper_title: Split-RL: Local Conflict Resolution in Reinforcement Learning
